analysis.title: Lev Fin Weekend Reading + Observations - beta blockers (KC O'Connor, 8 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Democrats took Congress and a majority of governorships in Tuesday's midterms. Markets rallied Wednesday, then reversed Thursday on concerns about data center development and more oversight of the AI build-out. $2.5tn of Nasdaq market value was erased on Thursday and GS's Vol Panic Index hit 9.57 out of 10, the third largest daily jump ever.
Credit decoupled from equities. The S&P 500 lost 2.7% on the week, but IG closed 1bp wider, HY closed 4bps tighter, and loans had their best weekly gain since April.

Wednesday was the best single day for HY in roughly seven months. On Thursday, the S&P's largest one-day drop since April 2025, cash spreads gave back Wednesday's gains, but CDX HY fell only 0.75pt against the 1.45pt move the S&P implied, a 2.7 standard-deviation outlier.
On the 10 days since 2018 with an S&P move as large as Thursday's, CDX HY's median move was -2.25pts, three times Thursday's loss, and it never lost less than it did Thursday.

Generic HY secondary levels stayed supported and produced the largest HY issuance total in five weeks. The 8 issuers that came saw their debt trade up an average of 1.1pts, with all 10 tranches higher in the aftermarket.

Hyperscalers sold five bond deals totaling $67bn over six business days, taking their YTD global debt issuance to $296bn against GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250bn. Oracle's new 5y tranche closed Friday at a 7.5% yield, above 83.8% of the 989 bonds in the HY double-B index.

The double-B to IG spread gap is 114bps, in the 92nd percentile since April 2025 and 46bps wider than late-August tights. GS reads this as the market pricing some IG AI supply as though it is high yield, rather than double-Bs being rich. The technical bid for higher-quality HY should continue for non-AI, non-energy, non-triple-C risk.
Weakness sat at two ends of the macro story. Data-center debt sold off on oversight concerns and energy bonds fell as the Iran war looked closer to ending. AI did more damage to the index.

Energy credit: only 20% of energy bonds rose versus 68% across HY, for a -0.28% sector return. HY energy widened 24bps while the index tightened 4bps. Energy is 11.4% of HY ($168bn, 230 bonds) and 14.3% of BBs. Each 100bps of energy widening costs the HY index about 0.38pt and BBs about 0.51pt.

AI/data-center credit: the 29 HY AI bonds traded at GS fell an average 1.67pts while the rest of HY rose 0.36pt. Within double-Bs the average AI bond fell 1.52pts, about 4.5x the 0.34pt decline in BB energy. Data-center bonds are 6.7% of the double-B index versus 14.3% for energy, but cost the index twice as much last week (-0.10pt vs -0.05pt).

GS takeaway: credit held up far better than its equity beta implied, but single-name dispersion remains near highs and software and building products are in their own micro cycles. The maturity wall is the slower problem, with 2028 HY bonds carrying a 5.9% average coupon against a 6.9% index median yield and 12.9% for triple-Cs. The weakest credits accounted for 11 of last week's 13 five-point decliners.

Loan market: only $28.2bn of new institutional loan deals launched in October, about half of September. Refinancings were 9.59% of the total, the lowest share since September 2022. 16 issuers YTD moved dollars from bonds to loans mid-syndication as issuers and sponsors favor prepayable paper.

Distressed leveraged loans (priced below $80) have nearly doubled since YE25 and are near their highest in over six years. The ICE BofA US Distressed Index underperformed the broader US High Yield Index by nearly 20% YTD through October, showing wide dispersion in lower-quality credit.

Of 41 local races with a data center moratorium, regulation or specific project on the ballot, voters came out against data centers 40 times. GS economists see short-term data center moratoriums as possible in the near term, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center expansion.

Chart of the week: since 1952 the 12 months after a midterm election have been the strongest stretch of the four-year cycle for the S&P 500. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over the next 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both the 6 and 12 month marks in all 18 instances.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit held up far better than its equity beta implied. CDX HY lost 0.75pt against the 1.45pt the S&P implied, HY was 4bps tighter on the week, and the technical bid for generic higher-quality HY is expected to continue.
tension_points.bear_case: Single-name dispersion remains near highs, distressed loans have nearly doubled since YE25, and the weakest credits accounted for 11 of 13 five-point decliners. The 2028 maturity wall means repricing from a 5.9% average coupon against a 6.9% median yield, and 12.9% for triple-Cs.

tension_points.bull_case: Double-Bs may be rich, with Oracle's 7.5% 5y yield above 83.8% of double-B bonds, which would make the IG AI paper look in line.
tension_points.bear_case: AI supply may simply be cheap. The double-B to IG gap is in the 92nd percentile since April 2025 and the market is pricing some IG AI supply as high yield, while hyperscaler issuance of $296bn already exceeds the $250bn full-year forecast.
